business.description: Cineline India Limited, through its flagship brand MovieMAX, operates as a national multiplex operator delivering premium yet accessible cinema experiences across India. The company follows a capital-light expansion strategy through Operations and Maintenance (O&M) partnerships and revenue-sharing models.

products.name: Convenience fee
products.note: Convenience fee is recognised as and when the movie tickets are sold on digital platforms. In case of fixed contracts with digital ticketing partners, revenue is recognised on accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

products.name: Virtual print fees
products.note: Revenue is recognised on an accrual basis in accordance with the terms of the relevant agreements.

products.name: Gift vouchers
products.note: Non-refundable Gift cards and vouchers are sold to customers. The prepayment amount received is recognised as unearned revenue liability. Revenue recognised in proportion to the pattern of rights exercised by the customer.

products.name: Rental Income
products.note: Revenue from rent and common area maintenance is recognised based upon the agreement, for the period the property has been let out.

products.name: Gaming income
products.note: Revenue from gaming is recognised as and when the games are played by customers.

outlook.statement: The outlook for India's film exhibition industry remains positive, with an extensive pipeline of film releases, continued multiplex expansion and sustained audience demand for theatrical entertainment. Continued growth in regional cinema, improving content quality and increasing investment across the media and entertainment ecosystem are expected to shape the industry's long-term growth.
The industry also remains on track to surpass ₹15,000 crore in annual box office collections, supported by a strong release calendar in the second half of the year.

As we enter the next phase of growth, our priorities remain clear: expand responsibly, enhance customer experiences, strengthen operational excellence and create enduring stakeholder value. A debt-free balance sheet, differentiated offerings and disciplined growth approach position us to capture emerging opportunities in India's cinema exhibition landscape.

Cineline enters FY 2026-27 with a strengthened financial position and a clear roadmap for long-term growth. Following its transition to a debt-free Company, it is well placed to accelerate its expansion through a capital-efficient model.
Aims to reach 105-110 screens by FY 2026-27 with a secured pipeline of 20-25 additional screens, focusing expansion in high-growth markets particularly South & North India.
Future screen additions will primarily be pursued through revenue-sharing arrangements, joint investments with developers and the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) model.
India's movie and entertainment market was valued at USD 6,311.2 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 14,881.6 million by 2034, registering a CAGR of 9.70% during 2026-34.
Domestic box office collections increased 21% year-on-year during the first half of 2026, reflecting healthy audience engagement.

risks: Rising trade tensions and outbreak of conflict in the Middle East affecting commodity markets, inflation expectations and financial conditions
Weaker expansion across several major economies in emerging markets
Softer domestic demand and continued adjustments in the property sector in China
High Fixed Cost Structure: Fixed lease commitments may impact profitability during periods of lower occupancy
Capital Investment Risk: High capital expenditure requirements may constrain expansion and affect returns
Content Performance Risk: Fluctuations in film performance may impact footfalls and box office collections
Technology and Consumer Preference Risk: Rapid changes in technology and evolving customer expectations may affect competitiveness
Credit risk from cash and cash equivalents, deposits with banks, security deposits, loans given and trade receivables
Liquidity risk managed through rolling forecasts and committed credit facilities
Market risk - interest rate risk on variable rate borrowings (though no variable rate borrowing outstanding)
Statutory impact of new Labour Codes effective 21 November 2025
